phase3_findings.description: The historical release-note entry for the earlier save_queries change, at line 73 of docs/external/release-notes.md, still says that SQL Lens "still saves free-form notes" when save_queries is off. This change removed exactly that clause from the matching row in docs/external/configuration.md, so the release-notes copy now states a promise the code no longer keeps. The line sits in a dated historical entry and the diff does not touch it. The two reviewers filed it with different kinds (documented_falsehood and comment_drift) but describe the same defect at the same file and line.

A blank or whitespace-only value for save_text_memories is turned into false with no log line or warning, at lines 221 to 230 of src/sqllens/config.py. An operator whose launcher expands an unset shell variable into SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES therefore gets note saving switched off silently, while a plain typo such as ture still fails loudly. The one case where the operator's intent is unclear is the one case with no diagnostic.

The internal readiness page docs/internal/production-readiness-v0.1.0.md, at line 70, still records that SaveTextMemoryTool is registered as a settled fact. After this change the tool is registered only when save_text_memories is on, so the unqualified sentence no longer holds for a default configuration. The file is a dated, point-in-time page and is outside this diff.

Line 30 of mcpb/manifest.json maps the environment variable to ${user_config.save_text_memories}. If an upgraded bundle install that has no stored value for this newly added field passes the placeholder through unreplaced, config loading raises a validation error and the server does not start, rather than falling back to off. The same shape already exists for read_only, so this is an existing pattern rather than something this change introduced.

The new tests at lines 253 to 276 of tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py assert only that the tool is absent and that the prompt section is missing. They do not pin the two further promises the factory comment makes for the flag-off path: that stored notes are still injected into the prompt, and that curated writes through MemoryStore.save_text_memory still go through. Those are the exact regressions the comment warns a future refactor could cause.

The test test_memory_admin_and_insecure_auth_are_not_exposed, at lines 51 to 61 of tests/unit/test_mcpb_manifest.py, pins the absence of settings unrelated to the behavior this change adds. It will fail and need editing on the day an unrelated change legitimately adds an admin-tools checkbox, with no real regression behind the failure. This is a maintenance cost rather than a defect.
